antibodies to mucin core protein epitopes are the most promising targets for the development of new serum assays for breast cancer detection.

The main takeaway from our work is that
different mucin epitope structures can be detected by different antibodies, and that the use of combinations of antibodies in a serum assay can increase its sensitivity and specificity.

the mucin glycoepitope recognized by antibody M29 is a better target for a serum assay for breast cancer than is the mucin glycopeptide recognized by antibody W1 or the mucin glycolipid recognized by antibody M26.
the best test for serum assays of mucins will probably be a combination of two or more antibodies.
